_metadata.description: COSMIC SBS mutational signature endpoints for ExposoGraph 2.0 carcinogen classes
_metadata.manuscript_context: v6 Discussion: linking ExposoGraph 2.0 predictions to tumor mutational signatures represents an important future direction
_metadata.confidence_notes: High-confidence entries have direct experimental and epidemiological attribution to the listed aetiology; medium-confidence entries are associations reported in at least one pan-cancer analysis; exploratory entries are hypothesis-generating.

SBS4.description: Attributed to direct DNA damage by polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in tobacco smoke; prevalent in lung (squamous and adenocarcinoma), larynx, and head & neck cancers.

SBS92.dominant_mutation: C>T at TpC and T>C at TpC
SBS92.description: Second tobacco-associated signature identified in bladder urothelial carcinoma, attributable to smoke-derived carcinogens excreted in urine.

SBS29.description: Found in oral cavity tumours of tobacco chewers; linked to tobacco-specific nitrosamines (NNK, NNN) and HCA-like agents.

SBS24.dominant_mutation: C>A, particularly at CpG with strand bias
SBS24.description: Signature of AFB1-induced N7-guanine adducts; characteristic of hepatocellular carcinomas from aflatoxin-endemic regions.

SBS22.description: Highly specific T>A transversions caused by aristolactam-DNA adducts; common in urothelial and hepatic cancers in East Asian populations.

SBS16.description: Associated with chronic alcohol consumption and ALDH2 deficiency; observed primarily in hepatocellular and esophageal squamous carcinoma.

SBS11.description: Canonical alkylator signature associated with O6-methylguanine adduct formation; amplified when MGMT is silenced.

SBS2.description: AID/APOBEC family deamination; indirectly amplified by inflammation and viral / oxidative-stress contexts including benzene toxicity and CHIP.

SBS13.aetiology: APOBEC cytidine deaminase activity (co-occurring with SBS2)
SBS13.description: Kataegis partner of SBS2; same upstream aetiology as SBS2.

SBS18.description: Mitochondrial and cytosolic ROS produce 8-oxoguanine lesions; linked to heavy-metal (Cr VI, Cd) exposure and benzene metabolites.

SBS88.description: Microbially produced colibactin crosslinks; implicated in colorectal and appendiceal cancers from gut-microbiome exposure.

SBS42.description: Associated with occupational exposure to chlorinated solvents (e.g., trichloroethylene) in cholangiocarcinoma and kidney cancer.

PAH.notes: Primary tobacco-smoke signature; SBS92 in urothelial lineage; SBS18 when oxidative stress dominates.

Tobacco_PAH.notes: Alias grouping for tobacco-derived PAH exposure.

Nitrosamine.notes: SBS29 for smokeless tobacco / NNK; SBS11 when MGMT silenced.

NDMA.notes: N-nitrosodimethylamine yields O6-methylguanine adducts; SBS11 canonical.

HCA.notes: HCA attribution shares N-hydroxy-arylamine chemistry with tobacco-specific nitrosamines.

AromaticAmines.notes: 4-ABP / benzidine adducts overlap with HCA / tobacco signatures.

Benzene.notes: ROS and APOBEC-like secondary activation reported in benzene exposure studies.

HeavyMetal.notes: Cr(VI), Cd, Ni act primarily through oxidative-stress ROS generation.

Dioxin.notes: Dioxins act mainly as AhR-mediated amplifiers rather than direct mutagens.

Estrogen.notes: Catechol-estrogen quinones generate ROS; no dedicated endogenous SBS signature in COSMIC.

Colibactin.notes: Gut microbiome colibactin exposure; colorectal / appendiceal.
